# NL-EDIT: Correcting Semantic Parse Errors through Natural Language Interaction

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#nl-edit)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2021.naacl-main.444.pdf) · NAACL 2021 proceedings, pages 5599-5610

**Reading coverage:** All 12 PDF pages: Sections 1-9, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-6, Figures 1-5 with captions and references. No appended supplement in this version.

## Research question

Correct an erroneous SQL parse from free-form feedback grounded in the original question, schema and query explanation.

## Method

Represents changes as clause-level add/remove operations and predicts linearized edits using BERT, relation-aware encoding and a Transformer decoder. Synthetic mutation-feedback pairs pretrain the model before SPLASH fine-tuning.

## Evaluation

One supplied feedback turn on SPLASH and additional EditSQL, TaBERT and RAT-SQL errors. Exact-set-match correction is accompanied by relative edit reduction; the representation discards condition values and restricts subquery structure.

## What the results support

Correction accuracy rises from 25.16% to 41.17%; errors decrease for 72.41% of examples but increase for 16.93%. End-to-end gains shrink as the base parser improves, from 20.3 points for Seq2Struct to 4.3 for RAT-SQL.

## Limits and qualifications

Recorded one-turn corrections do not establish multi-turn convergence. Longer explanations and irrelevant extra edits remain failure modes; edit-distance improvement is a structural proxy rather than complete semantic validation.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A useful feedback-integration baseline, with explicit evidence that editing can damage previously correct query components.
